summary: Latency regression (p95) after upgrading Dedicated cluster from serving-runtime 1.17.4 -> 1.18.0
description:
Customer (Quantgrid) reports a significant latency regression after upgrading their Dedicated runtime image from 1.17.4 to 1.18.0.

Issue summary
- After upgrade, p95 end-to-end latency increased 35–60% on steady workload.
- p50 stayed roughly flat (or slightly worse), but tail latency increased materially.
- The regression is most visible during mixed prompt-length traffic and when concurrency > ~0.8x reserved throughput.

Impact
- Customer SLO is driven by p95. Their upstream service sees request timeouts and queue buildup.
- Customer is asking for immediate rollback guidance and a way to pin runtime versions to avoid future forced upgrades.
- This ticket is being referenced internally as a key motivator for establishing an LTS channel (stability + predictable patch cadence).

Environment
- Dedicated cluster: qg-dedicated-prod (us-east)
- Runtime versions:
  - Baseline: serving-runtime 1.17.4 (good)
  - Current: serving-runtime 1.18.0 (regressed)
- GPUs: H100 80GB (8x nodes), autoscaling enabled (min 6, max 10)
- Models: llama-3.1-70b-instruct (primary), mistral-large-2407 (secondary)

Customer-observed symptoms
- Increased scheduler queue time and increased time-to-first-token (TTFT) at p95.
- Spikes correlate with bursts of short prompts mixed with occasional 8–16k context requests.
- No corresponding increase in 5xx, but client-side timeouts increased.

Steps to reproduce (customer)
1) Upgrade runtime image from 1.17.4 -> 1.18.0 on Dedicated.
2) Send mixed workload (roughly 70% short prompts < 512 input tokens, 25% medium 2–4k, 5% long 8–16k) at sustained concurrency.
3) Observe p95 latency over 30–60 minutes.

Evidence / snippets
- Customer sample request IDs (from their app logs):
  - req_01HQ9P7W2J6F0ZJ1G3W4H7Z1C0 (TTFT 1.9s, total 9.8s, runtime=1.18.0)
  - req_01HQ9P8D8E5JQY3N7N1Z9E3B2A (TTFT 2.3s, total 11.2s, runtime=1.18.0)

- Runtime logs (redacted) provided via Support upload (timestamp window 2025-01-20T18:02Z–18:40Z):
  - "scheduler_queue_delay_ms": p95 820 -> 1450
  - "prefill_ms": p95 640 -> 690
  - "decode_ms": p95 4200 -> 5200
  - "batch_fill_ratio": increased variance on 1.18.0 (more small underfilled batches)

- Dedicated metrics comparison (internal):
  - 1.17.4: p95 end-to-end 6.1s, TTFT p95 1.2s
  - 1.18.0: p95 end-to-end 9.4s, TTFT p95 2.1s

Asks from customer
- Immediate: rollback guidance and confirmation of safety.
- Short-term: ability to pin runtime version (and rollback quickly) without engaging support every time.
- Medium-term: stability channel with slower-change updates (LTS) + clear backport policy.

Initial hypothesis (internal)
- A change in batching/scheduling heuristics in 1.18.0 may increase tail latency under mixed prompt lengths.
- Possible interaction with autoscaling warm-up and queueing/backpressure behavior.

Proposed mitigation
- Rollback to 1.17.4 on Dedicated (customer-approved window), or disable the new batching heuristic if a safe flag exists.
- Track fix to either (a) revert/guard heuristic in a patch line, and (b) ensure perf-gate coverage for mixed prompt workloads prior to release.

Notes
- This is not currently reproducible on Hosted with the same magnitude (likely due to different routing + capacity headroom), but Dedicated sees it due to pinned capacity and workload shape.

resolution:
Mitigated by rolling Quantgrid Dedicated back to serving-runtime 1.17.4 (restored baseline p95 latency). Root cause suspected to be a 1.18.0 batching/scheduling heuristic increasing tail latency under mixed prompt lengths.

Follow-ups tracked outside this ticket:
- Add/strengthen perf gates for release/LTS branches (mixed prompt-length tail latency, queue delay thresholds).
- Provide runtime version pinning/rollback support as part of Runtime LTS rollout and Dedicated operational tooling.

Customer comms:
- Advised customer to stay pinned on 1.17.4 until a stability-focused patch/LTS option is available, with release notes and rollback guidance.
